h1: The 7 Best E-Readers With Stylus Support for Reading and Note-Taking, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: E-Readers With Stylus Support: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 e-readers with stylus support from Kindle, Kobo and BOOX, compared on screen size, color E Ink, pen included and Android.
summary: The Kindle Scribe Essentials Bundle is the best e-reader with a stylus for readers in the Amazon ecosystem, with a Premium Pen, PDF markup, notebook export and 64GB. The Kobo Libra Colour is the best for reading with occasional notes, the BOOX Go Color 7 gives open Android, and the Penstar eNote2 is the cheaper notebook-style tablet.
intro: E-readers with stylus support fall into two camps that look alike on a shelf. One is a reader that lets you scribble in the margins. The other is a digital notebook that also opens books. Which camp a device belongs to decides how it feels: a reader keeps page turns and book stores central, and a notebook puts pen latency and exports first. Decide whether you read more than you write before you choose.

We ranked seven devices that include or accept a stylus, from 7 inch color readers to a 10.3 inch notebook. Screen size, color E Ink, open Android and whether the pen is in the box shaped the order. One model does not include its pen, which we flag clearly.

products.name: Kindle Scribe Essentials Bundle (64GB) - Tungsten, Premium Pen, Leather Folio, Power Adapter
products.verdict: A Kindle with a Premium Pen, PDF markup, notebook export and 64GB storage in a bundle.
products.description:
The Kindle Scribe Essentials Bundle includes the 64GB Kindle Scribe in Tungsten, a Premium Pen, a leather folio and a power adapter. It supports PDF markup and notebook export. It costs $500 and up.

It wins for readers who already buy from Amazon because the store, library and writing tools sit in one device. PDF markup lets you annotate documents and exports send notes to your account or email. The folio and pen are in the bundle, so nothing else is needed. It is a closed system, with no open Android apps.

Buy it if you read on Kindle and want to write. Choose BOOX for other apps.
pros: Folio and adapter in the box
products.idealFor: Kindle readers who also want to write.

products.name: Kindle Scribe Essentials Bundle - Kindle Scribe Colorsoft (64GB), Premium Pen, Executive Folio
products.verdict: Color E Ink with note-taking, a Premium Pen and an Executive Folio in the bundle.
products.description:
This bundle pairs the Kindle Scribe Colorsoft with 64GB, a Premium Pen and an Executive Folio. It combines color E Ink with note-taking. It costs $500 and up.

Color lets you read covers, charts and highlight in several hues. It ranks second because color E Ink is softer and slower than grayscale, and the price sits above the standard Scribe. The writing tools match the first pick.

Buy it if you need both color reading and a pen. If you read novels, grayscale is enough.

products.name: Kobo Libra Colour eReader (White with Stylus), 7" Colour E Ink Kaleido 3
products.verdict: A 7 inch color Kaleido 3 reader with page-turn buttons and a stylus included.
products.description:
The Kobo Libra Colour has a 7 inch Colour E Ink Kaleido 3 display, physical page-turn buttons and a stylus in the box. It costs $200 to $500.

Page-turn buttons let you flip pages one-handed, which many readers prefer over swiping. The stylus handles annotation without turning the device into a notebook. It ranks third because note-taking tools are lighter than on the Scribe.

Buy it if reading is the priority. Pick the Scribe for heavy writing.

products.name: BOOX Go Color 7 Gen II Stylus Bundle
products.verdict: A color E Ink device with a stylus and genuine open Android for any reading app.
products.description:
The BOOX Go Color 7 Gen II comes in a bundle with a stylus and runs open Android on a color E Ink screen. It costs $200 to $500.

Open Android means you can install Kindle, Kobo, Libby and other apps on one device. It ranks fourth because Android on E Ink needs tuning and the experience is less polished than a dedicated store.

Buy it for app flexibility. Choose Kobo for polish.
products.skipIf: You want a simple closed system.

products.name: Bigme B751C Color eReader, 7" Eink Note-Taking Tablet with Stylus, Protective Case
products.verdict: A 7 inch color E Ink tablet with a stylus, protective case and open Android included.
products.description:
The Bigme B751C is a 7 inch E Ink note-taking tablet with color, a stylus, a protective case and open Android. It costs $200 to $500.

It ranks fifth because everything is in the box, though the brand is smaller than BOOX and software support is less certain.

Buy it for a complete package at a moderate price. Check update policy.
products.idealFor: A complete package at a moderate price.

products.name: Penstar eNote2 E-Ink Digital Notebook with Pen, 10.3" AI Note-Taking Paper Tablet
products.verdict: A 10.3 inch notebook with a pen and 8192 pressure levels, at an accessible price.
products.description:
The Penstar eNote2 is a 10.3 inch E Ink digital notebook with a pen included and 8192 pressure levels, with AI note features. It costs $200 to $500.

A larger screen suits handwriting and PDFs. It ranks sixth because it is a notebook first, with weaker reading and store support, and the brand is lesser known.

Buy it for note-taking and documents. Choose Kobo for books.

products.award: Best If You Own a Stylus
products.name: Musnap Ocean C 64GB+4GB 7" Color eBook Reader, Supports Handwriting
products.verdict: A 7 inch color Android reader with handwriting support, but the stylus is not included.
products.description:
The Musnap Ocean C has 64GB storage plus 4GB memory, a 7 inch color screen, open Android and handwriting support. The listing states the stylus is not included. It costs $200 to $500.

It finishes last because you must buy a compatible stylus separately, which adds cost and risk.

Buy it only if you already own a compatible stylus. Check compatibility.
products.skipIf: You want a pen in the box.

whatMatters.detail: A reader puts books first and pens second, a notebook the reverse. Decide which you use more. Screen size follows from that.
Some devices include the stylus, and one here does not. A separate pen adds cost and compatibility risk. Check the box contents.
Color suits covers and charts but looks muted and refreshes slower than grayscale. For novels, grayscale is sharper.
Open Android installs any reading app. A closed system is simpler but ties you to one store.
Notebook export and PDF markup let you move notes elsewhere. Check formats.

howToChoose.intro: Decide whether you read or write more.

cards.label: Closed ecosystem
cards.text: One store and a polished experience. The Kindle Scribe bundles and Kobo Libra Colour work this way.

cards.label: Open Android
cards.text: Install any app. The BOOX, Bigme and Musnap devices use it.

howToChoose.note: Choose closed for simplicity and open Android if you use several book services.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A large screen for PDFs, PDF markup, notebook export and a pen included.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Kindle Scribe bundle and the Penstar eNote2 are the best for study.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You write daily and want exports. The Kindle Scribe bundles at $500 and up deliver.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You mostly read. The Kobo Libra Colour at $200 to $500 does it well.

faq.a: Premium and many styluses need no battery. Check the specific pen. Replacement tips may be sold.
Assuming the stylus is included. The Musnap lists it as not included. Check the box.

faq.q: Is color E Ink worth it?
faq.a: For comics, charts and highlights, yes. For novels, grayscale is crisper.
Kindle Scribe exports notebooks to your account or email. Others export to files. Check formats.

faq.q: Can I use a Kindle app on BOOX?
faq.a: Yes, open Android installs the Kindle app. Performance varies.

faq.q: How long does the battery last?
faq.a: E Ink lasts weeks of reading, less with heavy writing and backlight. Listings here give no hours.

finalTake: The Kindle Scribe Essentials Bundle is the best e-reader with a stylus for Kindle readers who want to write. The Kobo Libra Colour is the pick for reading first, the BOOX Go Color 7 is the open Android choice, and the Penstar eNote2 is the large notebook. Skip the Musnap unless you own a stylus.
